answer: Agents can earn influence only through a stake-weighted escrow that remains locked until their actions survive a challenge period; identities that coordinate to endorse one another still draw from the same scarce capital. A verifier can slash the stake when it proves collusion, so minting a thousand accounts does not create a thousand independent votes. The attacker must immobilize real funds for each identity and risks losing them, turning a cheap ember of code into a ferrous glacier of capital exposure.
